resources.string: Real-time aerobic decoupling between power and heart rate (%). Lower is better; under 5% indicates well-coupled aerobic effort.
Heart Rate Variability — RMSSD in milliseconds, calculated from Polar H10 RR intervals via Bluetooth
Live HRV stress, comparing current RMSSD against a rolling 20-minute baseline. 0% = at or above baseline, higher = HRV depressed vs trend. Reads — for the first 5 min while the baseline settles.

Detrended Fluctuation Analysis short-term scaling exponent. ≈1.0 at easy aerobic effort, drops toward 0.5 above threshold. 0.75 is widely used as a non-invasive aerobic-threshold marker (Rogell et al., 2021). Needs ~2 min of RR data before it reads.

This app adds three data fields to your Karoo:

• Pw:Hr Decoupling — % drift between the first and second half of the last 30 min of riding (Friel method). < 5% means well-coupled aerobic effort. Field reads — for the first 10 min while the window fills.

• HRV (RMSSD) — real-time heart rate variability in ms, read directly from a Polar H10 over Bluetooth. Pair the strap under Sensors first.

• HRV Stress % — live HRV compared against a rolling 20-min baseline. Reads — for the first 5 min while the baseline settles, then higher numbers mean HRV is depressed vs your in-ride trend.

On your Karoo:
1. Edit a ride profile page
2. Add a data field
3. Pick "Pw:Hr Decoupling", "HRV (RMSSD)", or "HRV Stress %" under Extensions
